query: What learner needs and pain points appear in survey responses?

per_column.name: hands_on_exploration_need
per_column.rationale: A genuine axis for learner needs (physical/lab/manipulatives). But produced values are frequently unsupported: ED-0001 algebra 'camera freezes' yields 'manipulatives_absent' with no source basis; ED-0003 reading tears yields 'physical_materials_needed' though the text mentions only worksheets and logouts. Overfits hands-on labels onto non-hands-on complaints.

per_column.name: instructional_delivery_quality
per_column.rationale: Strong analytical leverage with well-differentiated delivery modes. Values track the text well: 'low_interactivity' for frozen whiteboard, 'no_live_discussion' for cameras-off silence, 'asynchronous_only' for recorded lectures. Sound readings.

per_column.name: attention_focus_sustainability
per_column.rationale: Useful engagement axis. However several values assert specifics the text does not support: ED-0003 'screen_fatigue_eye_strain' is unwarranted (child cries, no eye-strain cue); ED-0005 'attention_span_exceeded_20_min' invents a specific 20-min threshold not in the text. Contradicts groundedness.

per_column.name: household_equity_barrier
per_column.rationale: Equity is a strong, distinct analytical dimension. Grounded where evidenced (logouts as access issue), but ED-0001 'tech_access_unequal' overreads a single frozen camera as an equity gap, an unwarranted inference.

per_column.name: peer_interaction_loss
per_column.rationale: Clear, distinct axis. Values are well grounded: 'no_peer_discussion' for silent chat, 'social_isolation' for 'zero peer interaction', 'not_present' for silent rows. Sound overall.

per_column.name: subject_specific_challenge
per_column.rationale: Meaningful axis linking subject to modality challenge. But mislabels: ED-0005 discussion problem tagged 'literacy_group_needed' though it is essay participation, not literacy grouping; assignment somewhat conflates the subject column. Partial grounding failures.

judge.rationale: The six columns collectively give genuinely distinct analytical axes (hands-on need, delivery, attention, equity, peer loss, subject challenge) that all directly serve the query about learner needs and pain points, so usefulness is high with little redundancy. Groundedness is mixed: delivery and peer-interaction columns read the source text soundly, but several columns confidently assign specific labels the text does not support -- inventing manipulatives/physical-material needs, a 20-minute attention threshold, screen-fatigue, and equity gaps from thin cues, and mislabeling essay discussion as literacy grouping. These are the kind of confident specifics on silent or contrary text that lower groundedness.
